newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-BOGUS BOOKIE IN BIG EPSOM DERBY SWINDLE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BOGUS BOOKIE IN BIG EPSOM DERBY SWINDLE.

text.p: A bogus bookmaker has swindled an estimated 40,000 pounds ($65,000) from punters at Saturday's Epsom Derby after setting up with a fake permit and disappearing straight after the race.
Epsom's racecourse management has received 79 complaints about the bookmaker, who called himself John Batten, with registered claims for winning bets alone totalling over 10,500 pounds.
But the total stolen is expected to top 40,000 pounds as most of the bets were for the beaten favourite Entrepreneur.

The Sporting Life, a racing specialist newspaper, said on Wednesday eager punters were queuing up to take Batten's 6-4 against Entrepreneur who finished a poor fourth behind 11-1 Benny The Dip. Most bookmakers were only offering 6-4 ON Entrepreneur.
"Most of the complaints are coming from punters who put five pounds each way on Benny The Dip," a United Racecourses spokeswoman said.
"The matter is now firmly in the hands of Epsom local police," she said, adding that a punter captured Batten on a video of his day at the Derby and had handed police the tape.

Stephen Wallis, Epsom's racecourse manager, said Batten bought a bookmaker's badge and "flashed" a bookmaker's permit. Batten produced plausible betting tickets, although his code name of "Lucan" -- the fugitive peer who allegedly bludgeoned the family's nanny to death -- on the tickets could have aroused suspicions.
Both the address and the telephone number on the tickets turned out to be false.
